verdict.line: You lose this lane only if you facetank Volibear's empowered autos and let his passive attack speed ramp in a long trade; you win it the moment you bait his Q (Thundering Smash) into an empty Counter Strike (E).

brief.thesis: Volibear's only hard engage is the attack-based stun on Q (Thundering Smash), and Jax's E (Counter Strike) dodges all incoming basic attacks — including the one that carries that stun — which erases his all-in before it starts. That single interaction, plus Relentless Assault (R) giving Jax the better attack-speed curve in extended fights, is why Jax sits at 57.7% over 2617 games here despite only a 49.4% average top-lane win rate overall.

theirWindow.when: His Q (Thundering Smash) is off cooldown
theirWindow.what: Hold Counter Strike (E) and trigger it the instant he closes distance — the dodge voids the attack that carries his stun and stuns him right back instead.

yourWindow.when: His Q just went on cooldown (10-12s)
yourWindow.what: Extend the trade with Leap Strike (Q) into Empower (W) — with no stun to punish you, this is the window where standing and fighting favors Jax.

start.why: 56.4% win rate over 2163 games and the 65.8% pick — the raw AD and sustain let you match his early on-hit poke from W (Frenzied Maul) without losing the trade war.

boots.why: 58% win rate over 1092 games — Volibear's passive (The Relentless Storm) and W both rely on repeated basic attacks, and flat damage reduction from attacks blunts exactly that pressure.

core.why: The Sheen proc and stats power your Leap Strike (Q) into Empower (W) combo, closing the gap Volibear's early on-hit scaling tries to open.
Continues the Trinity path at 61.9% win rate over 373 games — more on-hit burst for trades you now win.
Completes the top core path; lets you commit to all-ins past his Stormbringer (R) engage window without dying to the follow-up.

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping attack speed stacks directly with Relentless Assault's (R) attack-speed steroid, maximizing damage in the exact extended trades this matchup's power curve hands you.

summoners.why: 57.3% win rate at 83.9% pick — Ignite punishes Volibear's W (Frenzied Maul) self-heal and converts your existing solo-kill advantage into actual kills.

playing.title: Bait the Q, answer with E
playing.detail: Never pre-emptively Counter Strike (E) — wait for Volibear to commit Thundering Smash (Q), then trigger E as he closes. It dodges the attack carrying his stun and stuns him instead.

playing.title: Cut trades short early
playing.detail: Volibear's passive stacks attack speed on every attack and ability use, so trades that go long favor him before level 6. Leap Strike (Q) in, Empower (W) auto, disengage.

playing.title: Watch for the double W
playing.detail: His W (Frenzied Maul) needs a second cast on the same mark to heal and burst — if he's already hit you once, back off or trade through it fast before the recast lands.

playing.title: Respect Sky Splitter's range
playing.detail: His E (Sky Splitter) reaches 1200 range and slows while shielding him if he's caught in it — don't walk straight lines or facecheck bushes when it's up (16s cooldown).

playing.title: All-in once R is up
playing.detail: Relentless Assault (R) has 0 base cooldown and rewards consecutive strikes — once it's available at 6, commit to extended fights instead of poking, since that's where your edge is largest.

playing.title: Track his ultimate's long cooldown
playing.detail: Stormbringer (R) starts at 160s and only drops to 110s at rank 3 — once he's spent it (gank setup or failed all-in), you get a long window to force skirmishes without fearing the leap engage.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why the Counter Strike/Thundering Smash interaction and the attack-speed trade pattern produce those numbers — is my own read on the matchup.
